cases.assessment: Relevant and readable with correct routing, but it repeats observations already supplied, weakly attributes a possible ignition diagnosis, and omits several first checks and explicit smoke, fuel-smell, heat, and leak stop conditions.
The altitude-specific three-minute value is correct, but the visible answer omits the ordinary one-minute boiling duration requested by the user and adds less relevant water-conservation material.
Strong prioritized STOP-style guidance, correct retrieval, and a useful condition on backtracking; weak semantic support correctly prevents a fully verified label.
Both generations failed the Lite response contract, so the user received only the retry message.
Directly gives the correct one-minute rolling-boil duration, safe cooling and storage, a contamination warning, and the correct Manual lesson with concise prose.
Readable but generic and ungrounded; it omits stopping and marking the last known point and could encourage movement without a known safe route.

summary.recommendation: Expert is currently more dependable across varied core prompts, while Lite is much faster and can be excellent on a clean retrieval hit. Neither tier is consistently reliable enough to treat this single smoke run as a release gate.
